text: David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-gedi.
When Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, "David is in the wilderness of En-gedi."
So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to look for David and his men in the direction of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
He came to the sheepfolds along the way, where there was a cave, and Saul went in to relieve himself. Now David and his men were sitting far back in the cave.

versions.text: He came to the sheepfolds along the way, where there was a cave, and Saul went in to relieve himself. Now David and his men were sitting far back in that very cave.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew simply reads "in the innermost parts of the cave"; "that very cave" adds an emphasis not present in the text. The plain wording also reads more smoothly aloud.

text: David's men said to him, "This is the day the LORD spoke of when he said to you, 'I am giving your enemy into your hand; do to him whatever seems good to you.'" So David got up and quietly cut off a corner of Saul's robe.
Afterward David's conscience struck him because he had cut off the corner of Saul's robe.
He said to his men, "The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my lord, the LORD's anointed, or lift my hand against him; for he is the LORD's anointed."
With these words David held his men back and would not let them attack Saul. And Saul left the cave and went on his way.
Then David got up, went out of the cave, and called after Saul, "My lord the king!" When Saul looked behind him, David bowed with his face to the ground and paid him homage.
David said to Saul, "Why do you listen to men who say, 'David is out to harm you'?

This very day your own eyes have seen how the LORD gave you into my hand in the cave. I was urged to kill you, but I spared you. I said, 'I will not lift my hand against my lord, for he is the LORD's anointed.'

Look, my father, see the corner of your robe in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe and did not kill you. Know then and understand that there is no evil or rebellion in my hand. I have not wronged you, yet you are hunting me down to take my life.

versions.text: Look, my father, see the corner of your robe in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe and did not kill you. Know then and understand that there is no evil or rebellion in my hands. I have not wronged you, yet you are hunting me down to take my life.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is singular ("in my hand"), matching the repeated "hand" imagery of the verse and chapter ("the corner of your robe in my hand"). The plural breaks that deliberate echo.

text: May the LORD judge between me and you, and may the LORD avenge me on you; but my own hand will not touch you.
As the old proverb says, 'From the wicked comes wickedness.' But my hand will not touch you.
Against whom has the king of Israel marched out? Whom are you chasing? A dead dog! A single flea!
May the LORD be the judge and decide between me and you. May he look into it, take up my cause, and vindicate me against your hand."
When David had finished saying this to Saul, Saul asked, "Is that your voice, my son David?" And Saul wept aloud.
He said to David, "You are more righteous than I, for you have repaid me with good, while I have repaid you with evil.
You have shown today how well you have dealt with me: the LORD handed me over to you, and you did not kill me.
When a man finds his enemy, does he let him go unharmed? May the LORD reward you with good for what you have done for me today.

versions.text: When a man finds his enemy, does he let him go unharmed? May the LORD reward you richly for what you have done for me today.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says "repay you with good" (טוֹבָה), which deliberately echoes the "good"/"evil" contrast running through verses 18-20. "Richly" loses that verbal link and adds a nuance the text does not have.

text: Now I know that you will surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be secure in your hand.
Swear to me now by the LORD that you will not wipe out my descendants after me or blot out my name from my father's house."
So David swore this to Saul. Then Saul went home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.
